en: To make a strong objection.
To affirm (something).
A formal objection, especially one by a group.
A collective gesture of disapproval; a demonstration.

protest.ety:

From the Middle English verb protesten, from Old French protester, from Latin prōtestārī, from prō + testor, from testis (“witness”).

ex.en: They held a protest march for freedom.
ex.ja: 彼らは自由を求めて抗議デモを行った。

ex.en: I cannot pass the matter by without making a protest.
ex.ja: 私は抗議もしないでそのことを大目にみることができない。

ex.en: He raised a finger in protest.
ex.ja: 彼は指を立てて抗議の意を示した。

en: The act of publishing printed or other matter.
An issue of printed or other matter, offered for sale or distribution.

publication.ety: From Middle English publicacioun, from Old French publicacion, from Latin pūblicātiō. By surface analysis, public + -ation.

ex.en: The book is now ready for publication.
ex.ja: 本は現在出版の準備が出来ている。

ex.en: He was in charge of preparing a magazine for publication.
ex.ja: 彼は雑誌の出版準備を担当していた。

ex.en: Publication of this month's issue will probably be delayed one week.
ex.ja: 今月号の発行は１週間遅れるだろう。

note.ja: publish（出版する）+ -cation。ラテン語 publicare（公にする）、publicus（公の）。「公にすること」→「出版」。

en: Free from sound or noise; absolutely still; perfectly quiet.
Not speaking; indisposed to talk; speechless; mute; taciturn; not loquacious; not talkative.
That which is silent; a time of silence.
A silent movie

silent.ety: From Latin silēns (“silent”), present participle of sileō (“be silent”), from Proto-Indo-European *seyl- (“still, windless, quiet, slow”). Related to Gothic 𐌰𐌽𐌰𐍃𐌹𐌻𐌰𐌽 (anasilan, “to cease, grow still, be silent”), Old English sālnes (“silence”).

ex.en: Not knowing what to say, I remained silent.
ex.ja: 何と言ってよいかわからなかったので、私は黙っていた。

note.ja: ラテン語 silens（黙っている）から。silere。「静かな・無言の」。

ex.ja: 彼はうまく新しい仕事を見つけることができた。

ex.en: She successfully got him to tell the truth.
ex.ja: 彼女はうまく彼から真実を聞きだした。

ex.en: Mr Smith carried out the plan successfully.
ex.ja: スミスさんはその計画を上手くやった。

note.ja: successful + -ly。「うまく」。

en: A house of worship dedicated to a polytheistic faith.
Synonym of synagogue, especially a non-Orthodox synagogue.
To build a temple for; to appropriate a temple to; to temple a god

temple.ety: From Middle English temple, from Old English templ, tempel, borrowed from Latin templum (“shrine, temple, area for auspices”). Compare Old High German tempal (“temple”), also a borrowing from the Latin. Displaced native Old English ealh.

ex.ja: 以前はちょうどここにお寺があった。

ex.en: There used to be an old temple here.
ex.ja: 昔はここにお寺がありました。

ex.en: That is the temple which they live in.
ex.ja: あれは彼らが住んでいる寺です。

note.ja: 「寺院」はラテン語 templum（神聖な場所）から。「こめかみ」はラテン語 tempora（こめかみ）からで別語。

en: To follow behind (someone or something); to tail (someone or something).
To drag (something) behind on the ground.
The track or indication marking the route followed by something that has passed, such as the footprints of animal on land or the contrail…
A route for travel over land, especially a narrow, unpaved pathway for use by hikers, horseback riders, etc.

ex.ja: 私には彼の凍った息が白く尾を引くのが見えた。

en: The brother or brother-in-law of one’s parent.
The male cousin of one’s parent.
A cry used to indicate surrender.
To address somebody by the term uncle.
To act like, or as, an uncle.

ex.ja: その子は叔父の名前をとってジョンと名づけられた。

ex.ja: ジョージ叔父さんは、家へ来る時はきっと何かお土産を持って来てくれました。

Something that is unusual; an anomaly.

ex.ja: 彼が早起きするなんて珍しい。

ex.en: The house stood out because of its unusual shape.
ex.ja: その家は珍しい形をしているので目につきやすかった。

note.ja: un（否定）+ usual（いつもの）。「珍しい」。

en: The act of arriving (reaching a certain place).
The fact of reaching a particular point in time.

arrival.ety: From Middle English arivaile, arivaille, arrival, arryvaile, arryvaylle, aryvayle, aryvaylle, from Middle French arrivaille, from arriver. By surface analysis, arrive + -al.

ex.en: Prior to your arrival, he left for London.
ex.ja: あなたが到着される前に、彼はロンドンへ出発しました。

ex.en: The news of her arrival excited the crowd.
ex.ja: 彼女の到着のニュースは群集を興奮させた。

ex.en: The party started soon after his arrival.
ex.ja: 一行は、彼が到着するとまもなく出発した。

note.ja: arrive（到着する）+ -al。ad + ripa（岸）。「岸に着くこと」→「到着」。

en: A violent onset or attack with physical means, for example blows, weapons, etc.
A violent verbal attack, for example with insults, criticism, and the like
To attack, physically or figuratively; to assail.
To threaten or harass.

assault.ety: From Middle English assaut, from Old French noun assaut, derived from the past participle of the verb assalir, from Late Latin assalīre, from Latin ad (“at, towards”) + salīre (“jump”). See also assail. Spelling Latinized around 1530 to add an l.

ex.en: The middle aged man was charged with assault.
ex.ja: その中年の男は暴行のかどで訴えられた。

ex.en: We were not prepared for the assault.
ex.ja: 我々はその襲撃に対して準備ができていなかった。

ex.en: We weren't prepared for the assault.
ex.ja: 我々はその襲撃に対して準備ができていなかった。

note.ja: as（〜へ）+ sault（跳ぶ）。〜へ跳びかかる →「襲撃・暴行」。

The state or quality of being aware of something.

ex.ja: 彼は明敏な問題意識をもっている。

note.ja: aware（気づいている）+ -ness。「意識・認識」。

en: In a bad manner.
Very much; to a great degree.
Ill, unwell.

badly.ety: From Middle English badly, baddely, baddeliche, equivalent to bad + -ly.

ex.en: We must always be prepared for the worst.
ex.ja: 我々は常に最悪の事態に備えていなければならない。

ex.en: Don't speak badly of him in his absence.
ex.ja: 陰で彼の悪口を言うな。

ex.en: To make matter worse, the traffic was bad.
ex.ja: なお悪いことに車の流れが悪かった。

note.ja: bad（悪い）+ -ly。「ひどく」→（want などと）「とても」。

en: A tub or pool which is used for bathing: bathtub.
A building or area where bathing occurs.
To wash a person or animal in a bath.
To bathe (oneself); to have a bath.

Cognate with Danish, Dutch, Norwegian, and Swedish bad (“bath”), Faroese and Icelandic bað (“bath”), German Bad (“bath”).

ex.en: His wife ran a hot bath for him.
ex.ja: 妻は彼のためにお風呂を用意した。

ex.en: I take a bath every morning in summer.
ex.ja: 私は夏には毎朝入浴する。

ex.en: I always take a bath in the morning.
ex.ja: 私は毎朝、入浴することにしている。

note.ja: 古英語 bæth から。「風呂」。動詞は bathe。

en: An act of capturing; a seizing by force or stratagem.
The securing of an object of strife or desire, as by the power of some attraction.
To take control of; to seize by force or stratagem.
To take hold of.

capture.ety: Borrowed from Middle French capture (noun), from Latin captūra. Displaced native Old English fenġ (noun) and ġefōn (verb).

ex.en: The boy captured the bird with a net.
ex.ja: 少年はその鳥を網で捕まえた。

ex.en: In the end, capture the stomach to win.
ex.ja: 結局、胃袋を掴んだもの勝ちだよね。

ex.en: The artist captured the charm of the lady.
ex.ja: 画家はその婦人の魅力をうまく捕らえた。

note.ja: cap（つかむ）+ ture。つかまえること →「捕らえる・獲得する」。

en: The act of one who chases another; a pursuit.
A hunt; the act of hunting; the pursuit of game.
To follow at speed.
To hunt.

chase.ety:

, see Norwegian skysse (“to hunt”).
Doublet of catch and related to capture. Displaced native Old English ōht, ēhtnes, and wāþ. Broadly overtook Old English huntaþ.
(to nag; to pressure): Likely influenced by 催 (ceoi¹, “to urge; to pressure”) and 追 (“to chase”), which are near-homophones.

ex.en: Chase the cat out of the kitchen.
ex.ja: 台所からその猫を追い出してくれ。

ex.en: The dog chased the cat up a tree.
ex.ja: 犬はネコを木の上まで追い詰めた。

ex.en: The dog lay panting after his long chase.
ex.ja: 長い間獲物を追いかけたのでその犬は寝そべってあえいでいた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 chacier から。ラテン語 captare（捕まえようとする）。catch と同じ語源。purchase にも含まれる。

en: A smaller, self-contained part of a larger entity. Often refers to a manufactured object that is part of a larger device.
A connected subgraph that is not part of any larger connected subgraph.
Making up a larger whole.
Made up of smaller complete units in combination.

component.ety: Borrowed from Latin compōnēns, compōnēntis, present participle of compōnō (“assemble, put together”).

ex.en: The components obtained by distillation of coal tar are as shown below.
ex.ja: コールタールを蒸留して得られる成分名は下表の通りである。

note.ja: ラテン語 componere ＝ com + ponere（置く）。「一緒に置かれたもの」→「部品・構成要素」。compose と同じ pon。

A building material created by mixing cement, water, and aggregate such as gravel and sand.
Such a material whose cement is Portland cement or a similar limestone derivative.
To cover with or encase in concrete (building material).
To solidify: to change from being abstract to being concrete (actual, real).

concrete.ety: Borrowed from Latin concrētus, past participle of concrescō (to curdle) from con- (with, together) + crescō (to grow, rise).

ex.ja: 計画を具体化することが難しい。

ex.en: Our plans are not yet concrete.
ex.ja: 我々の計画はまだ固まってない。

ex.en: A committee should apply the focus to the more concrete problem.
ex.ja: 委員会はもっと具体的な問題に焦点を当てるべきだ。

note.ja: ラテン語 concretus（固まった）から。con + crescere（成長する）。「固まった」→「具体的な」→「コンクリート」。increase と同じ cresc。

en: To a deep extent or degree; very greatly.
So as to extend far down or far into something.

deeply.ety: From Middle English deply, depely, from Old English dēoplīċe (“deeply”, adverb), from dēoplīc (“deep”), equivalent to deep + -ly.

ex.en: All the people felt for the victims deeply.
ex.ja: みんなが犠牲者達に深く同情した。

ex.en: I deeply appreciate your coming all the way.
ex.ja: はるばるおいでいただいて深く感謝いたします。

ex.en: I love him most deeply of all men.
ex.ja: 私はすべての男性の中彼を最も深く愛している。

note.ja: deep（深い）+ -ly。「深く」。

en: The act or state of expecting or looking forward to an event as about to happen.
That which is expected or looked for.

expectation.ety: From Middle French expectation, from Latin exspectātiō, from exspectō (“expect”). By surface analysis, expect + -ation. Displaced native Old English wēn.

ex.en: Your work didn't come up to our expectations.
ex.ja: 君の仕事は私たちの期待に添わなかった。

ex.en: I could not come up to his expectations.
ex.ja: 私は彼の期待にそえなかった。

ex.en: The new house didn't live up to expectations.
ex.ja: 新しい家は期待に添うものではなかった。

note.ja: expect（期待する）+ -ation。ex + spectare（見る）。「外を見て待つ」→「期待」。spectator と同じ spec。

en: The act or process of explaining.
Something that explains or makes understandable.

explanation.ety: From Latin explanatio (“an explanation, interpretation”), from explanare (“explain”); see explain. Morphologically explain + -ation. Displaced native Old English racu.

ex.en: I couldn't think up such a brief explanation.
ex.ja: そんな簡潔な説明は私には思いもつかなかった。

ex.en: His explanation proved to be right after all.
ex.ja: 結局、彼の説明が正しいと分かった。

ex.en: I shall want an explanation of your behavior.
ex.ja: 私は君の行いについて弁明を聞きたい。

note.ja: explain（説明する）+ -ation。ex + planare（平らにする）。「平らにしてわかりやすくする」→「説明」。plain と同じ。

Lack of protection from weather or the elements.

A verbal or written account that is not based on actual events (often intended to mislead); an untrue belief.

en: Anything that assures a certain outcome.
A legal assurance of something, e.g. a security for the fulfillment of an obligation.
To give an assurance that something will be done right.
To assume or take responsibility for a debt or other obligation.

guarantee.ety: From Old French guarantie (perhaps via a later Spanish garante), from the verb guarantir (“to protect, assure, vouch for”), ultimately from Old Frankish *warjand, *warand (“a warrant”), or from guaranty. Doublet of guaranty and warranty.

ex.en: I guarantee this watch to keep perfect time.
ex.ja: この時計は絶対に狂わないこと請け合いだ。

ex.en: This TV set has a two year guarantee.
ex.ja: このテレビは２年間の保障付きです。

ex.en: Some companies guarantee their workers a job for life.
ex.ja: 会社によって労働者は終身雇用を保証しているところもある。

note.ja: 古フランス語 garantie（保証）から。ゲルマン語 warjan（守る）。「保証」。warrant と同じ語源。

ex.en: I wish you great happiness in your marriage.
ex.ja: ご結婚おめでとうございます。

ex.en: It is generally believed that money brings happiness.
ex.ja: お金が幸福をもたらすと一般に信じられている。

note.ja: happy（幸せな）+ -ness。happy は hap（運）+ -y。perhaps、happen と同じ hap。

en: A thing that causes horror; a terrifying thing, particularly a prospective bad consequence asserted as likely to result from an act.
A person wearing a comic or grotesque costume in a parade of horribles.
Causing horror; terrible; shocking.
Tremendously bad.

horrible.ety: First attested in Middle English (alternately as horrible and orrible) in 1303: from Old French horrible, orrible, orible, from Latin horribilis, from horr(ēre) (“tremble”) + -ibilis (“-ible”).

ex.en: It was horrible to hear about the crime.
ex.ja: その犯罪は聞くも恐ろしいものだった。

ex.en: I will rescue you from these horrible circumstances.
ex.ja: 私がその恐ろしい状況からあなたを救ってやるぞ。

ex.en: It's horrible to get caught in rush hour traffic.
ex.ja: ラッシュアワーにでくわすのは最低だ。

note.ja: ラテン語 horribilis（身の毛がよだつ）から。horrere（毛が逆立つ）。horror と同じ。
